small_guidance:
- The inner loop iterates OUT_C=64 times redoing the same im2col gather for each oc; this is the dominant cost. Restructure as an outer loop over (kh, kw, ic) loading x once, then an inner loop accumulating into a register tile of shape (OUT_C, BLOCK_H*BLOCK_W) — or better, tile OUT_C with BLOCK_OC=16/32 and use tl.dot on a (BLOCK_OC, IC*KH*KW) × (IC*KH*KW, BLOCK_HW) GEMM.
- Add autotune configs with smaller spatial tiles but a BLOCK_OC dimension (e.g. BLOCK_H=8,BLOCK_W=32,BLOCK_OC=32 num_warps=4) so a register-resident min-reduction across OC tiles is feasible.
- Switch x to channels_last (NHWC) so the IC loop is the contiguous axis — current NCHW layout makes each ic load stride by H_IN*W_IN, wrecking L2 reuse across the 64 oc iterations.
large_guidance:
- Rewrite as an implicit-GEMM conv: one program tile computes a (BLOCK_HW, OUT_C) block by looping K = IC*KH*KW with tl.dot, then performs the min-reduction across the OUT_C axis in-register (tl.min along axis=1) and applies tanh(tanh(.)) in the epilogue before a single store of shape (BLOCK_HW,). This eliminates the OUT_C-fold redundancy (currently x is reloaded 64×) and uses tensor cores.
- Since output channels are fully reduced (min over all 64 OCs), keep OUT_C resident as a single BLOCK_N=64 tile — no inter-program reduction needed. Grid becomes (N, cdiv(H_OUT*W_OUT, BLOCK_M)); BLOCK_M≈64-128, BLOCK_K=IC*KH*KW=144 fits as one shot or two K-chunks.
- Convert input to NHWC once (cheap vs. 56ms), pre-reshape weight to (OUT_C, IC*KH*KW), and gather K-vector per output pixel via precomputed (kh,kw) offsets; this gives a clean coalesced GEMM-K and lets tl.dot do the heavy lifting.
